cards.explanation: The answer is that Gideon didn't call them to fight Midian. Ephraim's men ask, “Why did you fail to call us when you went to fight against Midian?” (Judges 8:1). That's the whole complaint, right there in the text. They felt left off the list, and they came to say so out loud. I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, so I know a little about being left out.

The answer is True. The text says it plainly: “And they contended with him violently.” (Judges 8:1). This wasn't a polite note in the suggestion box, friends. These men came in hot, and Gideon is standing right there in the middle of it.

The answer is Oreb and Zeeb, the princes of Midian. Gideon says, “God has delivered Oreb and Zeeb, the two princes of Midian, into your hand.” (Judges 8:3). Notice who he says did the delivering: God. Then he asks what he was able to do compared to them. That's a man handing out the credit instead of keeping it.

The answer is that their anger subsides. The text says, “When he had said this, their anger against him subsided.” (Judges 8:3). Gideon's answer took the fire out of the room. A few good words did what shouting never could.

The answer is bread, and exhausted. Gideon says, “Please give my troops some bread…” (Judges 8:5). He says his troops need it “…for they are exhausted…” (Judges 8:5), and the text says earlier that they crossed the Jordan exhausted yet still in pursuit (Judges 8:4). I know that tired, friends. It's the tired where even a crumb looks like a good deal.

The answer is False. The leaders of Succoth answer with a question: “Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna already in your possession, that we should give bread to your army?” (Judges 8:6). That question is what they give Gideon. They don't agree to give bread. So the statement is False.

The answer is when the LORD hands him the two kings. Gideon says, “when the LORD has delivered Zebah and Zalmunna into my hand…” (Judges 8:7). That's his timeline. He's saying that once the two kings are in his hand, he'll come back to Succoth. Notice he says the LORD is the one who delivers.

The answer is that they refuse him, just like Succoth. The text says, “…the men of Penuel gave the same response as the men of Succoth.” (Judges 8:8). Gideon asked Penuel for the same thing he asked Succoth. He got the same response. Two towns, one response.

The answer is their tower. Gideon tells the men of Penuel, “When I return in triumph, I will tear down this tower!” (Judges 8:9). The tower is the thing he names. And he says he'll do it when he returns in triumph.

The answer is one hundred twenty thousand. The text says, “A hundred and twenty thousand swordsmen had already fallen.” (Judges 8:10). Zebah and Zalmunna were at Karkor with about fifteen thousand men, all that were left of the armies of the people of the east. A hundred and twenty thousand swordsmen fallen, friends. Let that number sit a minute.

The answer is True. The text says Gideon “…attacked their army, taking them by surprise.” (Judges 8:11). He went up by way of the caravan route east of Nobah and Jogbehah to do it. I bet that army had no idea what hit it.

The answer is that Gideon captures them. The text says, “When Zebah and Zalmunna fled, Gideon pursued and captured these two kings of Midian…” (Judges 8:12). The kings fled, and Gideon pursued and captured them. Their entire army got routed too.

The answer is names. The text says the young man “…wrote down for him the names of the seventy-seven leaders and elders of Succoth.” (Judges 8:14). So Gideon walks away with a list. Seventy-seven names is a long list for one captured young man to write.

The answer is Zebah and Zalmunna. Gideon says, “Here are Zebah and Zalmunna, about whom you taunted me…” (Judges 8:15). These are the two kings Succoth said weren't in his hand yet. Now they stand right in front of the town.

The answer is False. The text says, “He also pulled down the tower of Penuel and killed the men of the city.” (Judges 8:17). So the tower does not stay standing. It's the tower Gideon had promised to tear down (Judges 8:9). This is a heavy part of the passage, and I won't make light of it.

The answer is men who looked like Gideon. The kings answer, “Men like you…each one resembling the son of a king.” (Judges 8:18). They say the men they killed looked like Gideon himself. It's a heavy answer for Gideon to hear.

The answer is brothers. Gideon says, “They were my brothers…the sons of my mother!” (Judges 8:19). That's who the men killed at Tabor were. I think this one hurts. He adds that if they had let them live, he would not kill them.

The answer is False. The text says, “But the young man did not draw his sword; he was fearful because he was still a youth.” (Judges 8:20). Jether, Gideon's firstborn, stood there with his sword put away. A young man, a hard order, and a heavy moment.

The answer is crescent ornaments. The text says Gideon “…took the crescent ornaments from the necks of their camels.” (Judges 8:21). The kings' camels were wearing them. It's a small detail, and the text puts it right at the end of the scene.
